R596.note: Removes @csrf_exempt (and its import) so CsrfViewMiddleware protects the POST again; method/auth branches, JSON shapes and the mailer call are byte-identical.

R597.note: Replaces mt_rand with bin2hex(random_bytes(32)); dropping the attacker-supplied client_seed removes no legitimate behaviour and the token still flows to the same UPDATE and mail().

R598.note: Pins ValidAlgorithms to HS256 on the existing TokenValidationParameters, the right API for this sink; the restriction is the fix itself for a SymmetricSecurityKey and the write-up states what to change if the issuer signs with HS384/512 (its asymmetric-key attack example is off-topic but harmless).

R599.note: toRealPath containment on the entry's parent closes the symlink escape before any bytes are written, but Files.createDirectories runs before that check, so a pre-existing symlink inside the destination lets an escaping entry create directories outside it, and the unconditional mkdir is a new on-disk side effect the original never had.

R600.note: getCanonicalPath containment against canonicalBaseDir + File.separator closes traversal after the second decode; the added startsWith("/") reject and the canonical check cannot refuse a legitimate flat attachment name, and headers/streaming are unchanged.

R601.note: The /bin/ls branch is closed, but the Windows branch still runs cmd.exe /c with the value as an array element and Java's WIN32 argument escaping does not escape &, so injection survives - reproduced on JDK 26 in a scratch dir: Runtime.exec(new String[]{cmd.exe,"/c","echo","x&ver"}) executed ver.

R602.note: Parameterized QueryRow with a ? placeholder; scan, error path and response formatting unchanged, and the write-up flags the $1 variant for PostgreSQL.

R603.note: Generic 500 body with the wrapped error sent to log.Printf instead; status code, defer f.Close() and the success path are untouched.

R604.note: Chains .RequireAuthorization() onto the MapDelete registration, the per-endpoint metadata this sink needs; nothing else in Program.cs changes and the new rejection of anonymous callers is the fix.

R605.note: Rejecting CR and LF before the socket write closes IMAP command injection at this raw-socket sink and cannot refuse a valid mailbox name; only nit is a null folder parameter now NPEs where it previously sent a literal 'null' SELECT.

R606.note: Setting CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler makes the raw cookie value the SPA echoes match what CsrfFilter compares, fixing the stated mismatch, but it silently drops the default XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler's BREACH masking (Spring's SPA recipe keeps XOR on render and only resolves raw) and the write-up misdescribes the default as failing to enforce validation.

R607.note: Containment via toRealPath + resolve + normalize + Path.startsWith closes the traversal and the existing catch/finally is preserved, but it adds a restriction the original accepted - any param containing a path separator is now rejected - and dropping URLDecoder.decode changes the target filename for a percent-encoded cookie value (that second change is at least stated).

R608.note: Secure: true closes the reported flag; the added HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax are stated hardening that blocks no legitimate use of a server-side session token, and the handler's flow is otherwise unchanged.

R609.note: FromSqlInterpolated parameterizes both tenantId and the pre-built %term% pattern, keeping the contains-style match, the tenant filter, the async List<Product> return and the empty-term behaviour identical.
